turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): In you come. It's the cough you've booked for?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Dry cough, and I had a cold, so I thought it was just that lingering. Mind you the wind on our road this week has been shocking.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, three weeks. No, wait, six weeks. It was already going before my sister's do, and that was six weeks ago. Wakes me a bit at night as well.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Every evening, Doctor. She coughs the whole evening.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any phlegm?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing comes up.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Breathless? Any chest pain?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Neither. I was washed out while the cold was on me, but that's gone.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which blood pressure tablet are you taking?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): For my high blood pressure, yes. Ramipril — no, enalapril, I always get those two muddled. Five milligrams, once a day, in the morning.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The box at home says ten milligrams. I'm sure of it.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Does it? I just swallow the one. I don't study the packet. Jean at the post office was saying her husband's on something similar.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did you start the enalapril?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, about a month ago. Well, actually, maybe five weeks. I can't pin the date.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It was the beginning of last month, after Dr Shah. And Uncle Terry takes lisinopril — he coughs too, that's what made me think.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's his tablet, not yours. Any wheeze?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No wheeze.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Swelling of the lips or face?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. The boiler was throwing dust about, I did wonder.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Smoke?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Packed it in years ago. One glass of wine at the weekend, if that.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Other medicines?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Paracetamol now and then for my knees. Not every day.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to anything?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure is one forty-eight over eighty-eight. Pulse seventy-six.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear. Throat looks mildly red. Ankles aren't swollen.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): So is it still the cold, then?
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not pinning it down. Could be the enalapril, could be the tail of that cold. I won't call it either today.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stop the enalapril. Start amlodipine five milligrams once a day instead.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine. My neighbour's ankles went up like balloons on that, she reckons.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): They can do. If the cough hasn't eased or the ankles swell in two weeks, come back. Otherwise I'll see you in six weeks.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks is fine. I'll tell Terry to put a sock in it. Thanks.
